purpose: Verify adjudicated candidates against the source text: is each candidate's claim actually present in the document (no hallucination), and are its condition/factuality labels consistent with the source?

method.source_text: The extraction run's own input segments, carried by the v6 payload `structure.segments` (10 segments, industrial-fulian-md).
method.why_not_corpus_db: The snapshot build `f16e7fde95537f0656a69cb1547232ca26a0347b3823d0dc1844dbf798149314` has 0 rows in `e6_holdout_corpus.corpus.corpus_units` (35 other builds present); probing for segment text across all builds also returns nothing. The corpus DB therefore cannot serve as the reference for this run.
method.lookup_validated_by_control: Before drawing conclusions, `coverage_by_judgement.py` showed `matched` quotes also failed to resolve in the corpus DB (1/26), proving the miss was an artefact of the reference source, not of the candidates.

outputs.check_correct_extra_in_source.py: first attempt (corpus-DB based); kept as the record of the rejected lookup
outputs.coverage_by_judgement.py: control: quote coverage grouped by judgement, proves the DB lookup was invalid
outputs.locate_source_units.py: probes for the source document across all corpus builds (0 hits)
outputs.verify_quotes_against_segments.py: authoritative check: quote-in-segment for all 222 candidates

findings.sample_15_note: All 15 mechanically-suspicious `correct_extra` records have their evidence quote literally present in a source segment; none is a hallucination.

quote_coverage_222.optical-module-docx: 0 hit — docx source segments were not available, so these 134 records are UNVERIFIED, not proven wrong

systemic_labelling_defect.disposition: content is true; the condition/qualifier label is wrong. This is a production-side labelling defect to record, NOT a reason to rewrite candidate text.
